physical.notes: Self Test: normally-open coin-door button A4J3-1 (R) to A3J2-7 (Y-R).

On-board S33 pushbutton pulls the 6800 NMI input low in the MPU circuit. PinMAME's generic CPU Diagnostic input asserts that NMI. The assembly drawing calls S33 MEMORY CLEAR. Its separate remote door contact at A4J3-5 is recorded outside the public matrix API; no equivalence of those two electrical paths is assumed.

The generic sound-diagnostic input is consumed by the ST300 st300_switch_w handler, which stores voiceSw for st300_ctrl_w; it is a meaningful emulator route. No fitted Seawitch sound-diagnostic button is established here. Do not infer physical fitment from that route.

Normally-open MEMORY CLEAR S33 contact on the cabinet sheet, A4J3-5 W to A3J2-7 Y-R. The MPU sheet labels J3-5 EXT. BOOKKEEPING RESET. It is distinct from matrix switches and the separately drawn on-board NMI pushbutton. This profile-local physical binding has no controller transport; no ROM effect is claimed from a host matrix write.

mechanisms.behavior: Targets [21, 22, 23, 24] run highest to lowest in player view. Each target drops independently, latching its normally-open switch closed. One common reset bar/coil raises the whole bank, opening its switches. The known script's bank initializer explicitly preserves this membership (the left/right arrays are listed in reverse object order). At game start the ROM resets all three banks. Completing this bank in the retained game pulses public 7; a host holds targets down until that reset and then releases them. Targets start up. Repeat reset attempts with a held switch or a ball remaining in the out-hole are documented ROM behavior, not extra reset actuators. A target stuck down or a jammed reset bar leaves its sensor closed; reproduce the physical feedback rather than clearing it on a timer. Bank completion spots the corresponding loop/extra-ball award and advances the bonus multiplier when its increase lamp is on. Physical reset-pulse width and target animation remain table tuning.
mechanisms.label: Center four-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: One ball and no storage trough. Drain routes the ball onto switch 33; initialize it occupied. Credit/start resets the three banks and kicks the out-hole until the ball leaves 33. Its physical eject feeds the shooter lane, where the player operates the manual plunger. The table's ballrelease kicker is the virtual destination of this feed, not another physical coil or switch. A ball still holding 33 produces repeat out-hole and bank-reset pulses; do not keep 33 closed after a successful serve. On drain the ROM counts bonus, advances player/ball and serves again; an earned extra ball is played immediately without advancing player/ball. Tilt suppresses that ball's bonus and flippers, returning to normal at the next serve. No powered plunger, shooter-lane sensor, multiball trough or eject-position feedback is fitted in these sources.
mechanisms.label: Single-ball drain, outhole and manual launch

mechanisms.behavior: Free-spinning target A-563-13, target/wire 14A-7-12. Each revolution closes switch 5 briefly; no coil or home sensor. Ball passes the spinner in the right runway. The four value lamps describe the ROM's value ladder; initial score is 200 plus 200 per lit value, up to 1,000 (manual p10).
mechanisms.label: Right spinner

mechanisms.behavior: Passive ball-operated roll-over button 4B-275. Normally open, closed while depressed; no actuator, latch or separate home sensor. The top button scores the lit loop value; the runway button adds 3,000 bonus and can collect special (manual p10).
mechanisms.label: Rear loop star roll-over

mechanisms.behavior: Two spring-return dual-winding flippers: one lower by the apron and one upper beside its target bank. The single cabinet button and flipper-enable relay supply the side's circuit. Four winding-bypass contacts (two per side) are drawn across hold windings, conducting at rest and opening at stroke; they are hard-wired and absent from MPU switch tests. Preserve the factory E.O.S. series marks literally rather than inventing another public channel. The retained table moves both flippers of the side on its one lower callback. PinMAME asserts both synthetic outputs together throughout an enabled button closure and does not simulate physical current, EOS staging or independent upper motion; mechanical stroke/return timing is table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Left lower/upper flipper pair

mechanisms.behavior: Ball-operated gate beside the upper-right flipper/runway, with no solenoid or sensor binding. The script's SLS/SLS2 handlers animate a one-way barrier from ball direction and passage, with no SolCallback. This is passive ball routing; do not invent a powered diverter or controller output. Gate travel speed in the table is a recreation parameter.
mechanisms.label: Passive runway gate
